source: R. A. Keys and S. K. Clubley, Experimental analysis of debris distribution of masonry panels subjected to long duration blast loading, Engineering Structures 130 (2017) 229-241, doi:10.1016/j.engstruct.2016.10.044 (accepted manuscript, Loughborough repository, figshare 9443321); construction details also from R. A. Keys, PhD thesis, University of Southampton, 2016
licence: Numbers only, transcribed from the paper's table 1 and text and read off its figures 14, 19 and 20; no text or figure is reproduced. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the trials' data are the property of the UK MoD. See README.md.

construction.brick: frogged London brick, 215 x 100 x 65 mm, about 2.1 kg, compressive strength 4-6 MPa
construction.edges: free at the top and both sides (unenclosed panels)

walls.name: BWL1A
walls.obstruction: two instrumentation columns at about 30 m piled the debris; without them the authors expect 30-50 m and a farthest throw of 50-60 m

walls.name: BWL2C
walls.obstruction: lights for the high-speed cameras at about 7 m piled the debris; without them the authors expect it spread over 6-12 m

walls.name: BWL3B
walls.obstruction: lights at about 7 m, as for BWL2C; the plot ends at 14.5 m with mass still in its last bin

notes: x is measured downstream from the structure's most upstream point (the front face); each value is the mass in the bin starting at index x binWidth, read off the total-mass curve to about 3 kg. Cracks: horizontal, along bed joints, seen at 50 ms (first visible at 10-15 ms). BWL3B formed 2-3 horizontal cracks at similar intervals plus vertical and stepped ones down its centre; its heights are not stated.
